title: Tibiofibular syndesmosis
summary: The distal tibiofibular joint is a syndesmosis; it is formed by the rough, convex surface of the medial side of the distal end of the fibula, and a rough concave surface on the lateral side of the tibia.
Below, to the extent of about 4 mm, these surfaces are smooth and covered with cartilage, which is continuous with that of the ankle joint.
Anterior ligament of the lateral malleolus Posterior ligament of the lateral malleolus Interosseous membrane of leg
The inferior transverse ligament of the tibiofibular syndesmosis is included in older versions of Gray's Anatomy, but not in Terminologia Anatomica.
However, it still appears in some anatomy textbooks.
